Software Acceptance and Support Agreement for the
Larkspur Dispatch Platform
This agreement records the binding understanding between Corvid Logistics Cooperative,
the licensee, and Tesselwick Software Studio, the licensor, concerning delivery, acceptance
and ongoing support of the Larkspur Dispatch Platform. It fixes the scope of licensed
modules, the acceptance procedure with its review periods, the support service levels and
the commercial terms for a term of 12 months. Both parties confirm that no other document
supersedes the obligations stated here.

1 Scope of Licensed Software and Deliverables
Table 1: Term, renewal and termination positions
The licensor shall deliver the dispatch scheduling module, the driver communications
module and the reporting console described in the delivery schedule, together with
installation notes, an administrator handbook and test data. Source code is held in escrow
but not transferred. The licensee receives a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence for use
at 4 operating sites. Any module not expressly listed remains outside scope and requires a
written change order signed by both parties.
1.1 Delivery Milestones and Acceptance Testing
Delivery proceeds in staged milestones so that the licensee can verify each module before
the next is installed. The licensor gives written notice when a milestone is ready, and the
licensee then runs the acceptance tests described in the test plan. Acceptance depends on
documented results, not on impressions. Milestone dates, responsible parties and the
evidence each party must produce are set out in the schedule of delivery obligations.

1.1.1 Acceptance Test Procedure and Evidence
The acceptance test procedure defines the test cases, the expected results and the
recording format. The licensee executes the cases on its own equipment and records
observations in a shared log. Each observation is tagged as a simulated test result rather
than a production measurement, and no causal claim about business outcomes may be
drawn from it. Discrepancies are logged with severity and reproduction steps.
Supporting records are presented in Table 2.
Table 2: Acceptance coverage areas with evidence and stance
1.1.1.1 Test Case Coverage and Pass Criteria
Pass criteria are agreed per test case before execution begins. A milestone passes when all
critical cases succeed and no open defect of the highest severity remains. The table below
summarises the coverage areas, the evidence required and the acceptance stance for each
area, so that reviewers apply the same standard across all 4 sites.
1.1.1.2 Defect Severity and Remediation Windows
Each defect is classified by severity at logging, and the licensor may contest the
classification only in writing within 2 days. Critical defects block acceptance until remedied.
The licensor must acknowledge every defect within 2 days and provide a remediation plan
for high-severity items. Retesting follows the same recording discipline, and closure
requires the licensee's written confirmation.
1.1.2 Acceptance Decision and Deemed Approval
The licensee issues an acceptance decision within 5 days of receiving the milestone notice
and test materials. The decision states acceptance, conditional acceptance with a defect
list, or rejection with reasons. Silence beyond the review period counts as conditional
acceptance only where the licensee has received complete test materials. Rejected
milestones are resubmitted with a fresh notice and a new review period.
SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT | RESEARCH PROTOTYPE
1.2 Outstanding Defects and Conditional Acceptance
Conditional acceptance allows operations to begin while listed defects are corrected. The
parties record each outstanding defect, its severity, the agreed correction date and any
interim workaround. Support obligations commence at conditional acceptance, but final
acceptance is withheld until the defect list is cleared or formally waived. Waivers must be
written and do not extinguish latent defect remedies.
2 Support Services and Service Levels
Following acceptance, the licensor provides support for the remainder of the term of 12
months. Support covers incident intake, diagnosis, workarounds and corrections within the
licensed scope. The service levels distinguish critical, high and routine incidents, each with
an acknowledgement target and a restoration target. Support excludes custom
development, third-party hardware faults and misuse, which are handled under separate
arrangements.
Supporting records are presented in Table 3.
Table 3: Support channels, availability and response expectations
2.1 Incident Handling and Escalation
Incidents are logged through the shared service desk with a unique reference and a
severity assigned at intake. The licensor acknowledges critical incidents within 2 days and
provides updates at agreed intervals until restoration. If progress stalls, the licensee may
escalate to the licensor's named service manager, then to the account director. Escalation
does not alter the underlying service level commitments.
2.1.1 Support Channels, Hours and Response Targets
Support is available through the service desk portal and a telephone line during agreed
business hours, with an out-of-hours route for critical incidents. Response targets are
measured from logged intake to first substantive reply. The table below sets out the
channels, the hours and the response expectations so that both parties share one
operational reference.

2.1.1.1 Response and Restoration Targets by Severity
Severity determines the urgency of the response and the restoration expectation. Critical
incidents receive continuous attention until a workaround is in place. High incidents are
worked during business hours with daily updates. Routine incidents are scheduled into the
normal release cycle. The table below records the targets and the reporting duty attached
to each severity band.
Supporting records are presented in Table 4.
2.1.1.2 Monthly Service Reporting and Review Meetings
Table 4: Severity bands with targets and reporting duties
The licensor submits a monthly service report covering incident volumes, response
performance against targets, open defects and planned maintenance. The parties meet
quarterly to review the report, confirm corrective actions and agree improvement priorities.
Reports distinguish logged observations from inferred causes, and no report may present
simulated figures as measured production outcomes without a clear label.
Supporting records are presented in Table 5.
Table 5: Incident escalation stages and responsibilities
2.1.2 Maintenance Windows and Change Control
Planned maintenance occurs in agreed windows notified at least 5 days in advance.
Emergency maintenance is permitted for critical security or stability matters, with notice as
SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT | RESEARCH PROTOTYPE
soon as practicable. Changes to the licensed software follow the change control procedure,
including impact assessment, rollback plan and post-change verification. Unapproved
changes that cause incidents are remedied at the licensor's cost.
2.2 Fees, Term, Renewal and Termination
Support fees are invoiced annually in advance and are payable within the stated period.
The agreement runs for 12 months and renews only by written agreement of both parties.
Either party may terminate for material breach that remains uncured after a written notice
period, or for insolvency. On termination the licensee receives a final data extract and
continued access for a defined wind-down period.
